plan: To preserve capital, sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero.
Trim QQQI to 20% to meet the single-name concentration limit.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a steady, low-drawdown profile by favoring income and broad index exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a potential ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to reduce overall leverage and concentration.
Buy LMT at 4% as a new, high-quality long setup from the scanner.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining some exposure to quality tech.
It aims for a more diversified portfolio with a moderate cash buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan targets a potential ~2.5%/month return, prioritizing risk-first growth. It reduces leveraged exposure while adding a high-quality name. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with a blend of broad market and quality tech exposure.

plan: Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to lean into growth.
Buy LMT at 6% as a high-scoring long setup from the scanner.
This plan aims for stretched growth by using leverage and concentrating in strong setups.
It requires strict stop discipline due to amplified upside and drawdown potential.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a potential ~4%/month return, aiming for stretched growth. It significantly increases leverage and concentration in high-scoring setups. Be aware that this strategy amplifies both upside and drawdown, and leveraged ETFs experience daily decay. Strict stop discipline is crucial to manage the higher risk.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, METU, MUU, PLTU, MSFU, SPAL) to zero to prioritize income and reduce risk.
Add to QQQI, targeting 30%, to increase exposure to income-generating assets.
This plan focuses on generating steady monthly distributions and minimizing drawdown.
It shifts the portfolio towards cash-like income, not growth.
income.read: This income plan targets a potential ~1%/month return, focusing on parking cash for yield. It eliminates leveraged and high-beta names, rotating into income-focused ETFs. While prioritizing low drawdown and reliable income, remember distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff.
